spec: DESIGN.md — installations, the machine seam, save locations
description: Whole fixture machines (files, dirs, symlinks, core answers) in; the canonical contract serializations (atlas/contract.py) out, asserted with exact equality: installations (kind, kinds, root, health issue codes) and — per query — the full SavefilePlacement (dir, root_kind, needs, fallback_dir, physical_dir, file_set incl. completeness, granularity incl. option identity and alternatives, caveat codes + data), catalogue entries, and entry-route outcomes incl. Unresolved. Prose (sources, messages) is non-contractual. Layout facts are sourced from RetroArch runloop.c/configuration.c/config.def.h and the shipped RetroDECK/EmuDeck configs; see docs/research/retrodeck-save-placement.md.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-content-concrete
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK stock layout: cfg sets savefile_directory and sort-by-content. With a content path given, the placement is concrete: saves/<parent-dir-name>/. The existing save is observed, not guessed.

vectors.name: retrodeck-multi-disc-m3u-folder
vectors.rationale: The multi-disc convention: the ROM's parent directory is named '<title>.m3u'. content_dir is the parent directory name (runloop.c:8781), so the save lands under saves/<title>.m3u/ — observed on a real installation.

vectors.name: retrodeck-core-override-flips-sort
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK ships config/PPSSPP/PPSSPP.cfg with sort_savefiles_by_content_enable=false — a stock installation where the core override flips the layout flat for PPSSPP-libretro. The override directory is keyed by library_name (PPSSPP), resolved live from the core binary.

vectors.name: retrodeck-game-override-wins-over-core-override
vectors.rationale: The chain stacks core → content-dir → game, later wins (configuration.c:7095). The core override turns sorting off; the game override turns it back on — the game override must win.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-core-resolves-library-name
vectors.rationale: Sorting by core appends library_name — the core's self-reported display name (mGBA), not the .so basename (mgba). Resolved live via query_core through the /app→Flatpak-deployment translation; the existing save is observed through it.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-core-without-core-leaves-hole
vectors.rationale: Sorting by core needs library_name; without a named core the hole stays open (a hole is not an unknown — the caller can fill it), and a caveat states that per-core overrides were not checked.

vectors.name: retrodeck-savefiles-in-content-dir
vectors.rationale: savefiles_in_content_dir: the save lives next to the ROM. With the content path given, the directory is the ROM's own folder, concrete.

vectors.name: retrodeck-root-missing-health
vectors.rationale: The commonest Steam Deck failure: retrodeck.json is readable but points at an unmounted SD card. Detection reports health=root_missing instead of handing out a syntactically correct path as if usable.

vectors.name: retrodeck-no-query-detection-only
vectors.rationale: Detection without a placement question: retrodeck.json present, root exists, health ok.

vectors.name: emudeck-flat-layout
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck: settings.sh is the truth, the bare org.libretro.RetroArch Flatpak is its RetroArch, the shipped layout is flat (sort keys false). One handle for both descriptions — no separate bare installation.

vectors.name: standalone-flatpak-upstream-default-sorts-by-core
vectors.rationale: RetroArch's upstream compile-time default is sort_savefiles_enable=true (config.def.h:982). A bare Flatpak whose cfg sets only the directory sorts by core — the placement needs library_name.

vectors.name: standalone-flatpak-savefile-directory-absent
vectors.rationale: An unset savefile_directory means the RetroArch platform default — 'saves' under the config tree (platform_unix.c:2133-2134) — never the ROM's directory; upstream compile defaults then sort by core.

vectors.name: native-explicit-flat-with-observed-multifile-save
vectors.rationale: A native install with sorting explicitly off; the existing save is a core-written multi-file set (Beetle Saturn's .bcr/.bkr/.smpc). The file set is observed, never derived from an .srm assumption.

vectors.name: unloadable-core-is-stated-not-guessed
vectors.rationale: A core that is present but unloadable (missing host library — the applewin case) yields library_name unknown: the hole stays open and the caveat states it. Never a guess from the .so filename. This core carries no card, so nothing was retired and no core-generation-unestablished rides here — core-unqueryable already says the read failed, and a second caveat would announce the loss of knowledge that never existed.

vectors.name: symlinked-save-dir-reads-through
vectors.rationale: A save directory reached through a symlink (RetroDECK's dir_prep pattern): the fixture resolves link prefixes like the kernel, so the observed file set is found through the link.

vectors.name: coexistence-retrodeck-and-native
vectors.rationale: Coexisting installations each get their own handle, RetroDECK first; no cross-installation fall-through and no silently chosen winner.

vectors.name: emudeck-claims-standalone-flatpak
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck is a configured org.libretro.RetroArch — the same RetroArch under two descriptions. One handle carrying both, never a second handle for the same installation.

vectors.name: emudeck-marker-paths-partially-quoted
vectors.rationale: What the app-driven installer actually writes: every path key quotes only its jq-read prefix (jsonToBashVars.sh:116-123 @ 863ab69) and source concatenates the segments into one word. The marker-derived root comes out quote-free and health does not false-alarm root-missing on a healthy machine — observed on a live EmuDeck installation.

vectors.name: nothing-installed
vectors.rationale: An empty machine detects nothing; an empty list is the truthful answer.

vectors.name: flycast-shared-vmus-in-system-directory
vectors.rationale: Flycast's default roots saves in system_directory, not savefile_directory: shared VMUs under <system_directory>/dc, one set for every game (rule card 'flycast', governing option reicast_per_content_vmus read live). Only the VMUs actually present are observed; granularity states the shared card and how to switch.

vectors.name: flycast-per-content-vmus-are-named-after-the-disc-id
vectors.rationale: reicast_per_content_vmus = 'All VMUs' writes one VMU per connected port into the save directory the frontend hands the core — the content-sorted one, no subdirectory of the core's own — named after the disc's product id (flycast@1dac369 oslib.cpp:38-67, libretro.cpp:2142-2148; live-verified on RetroDECK 0.10.9b). The id is written in the disc header, which atlas does not read: the file set is stated as the template it is and 'save_id' joins needs. Content without such an id — arcade, or a disc header stating none — is named after the ROM by the same function (oslib.cpp:62); atlas cannot decide which case it has, so 'filenames-content-conditional' carries both spellings, the alternative filled from the content path. A per-game VMU already lying in that directory is deliberately NOT attributed to this content — a content-sorted directory holds every game of one ROM directory, so reading a name back as this save would be a guess.

vectors.name: catalogue-declared-order-and-classification
vectors.rationale: The catalogue is read live from the bundled es_systems.xml in the Flatpak deployment: entries in declared order (first = ES-DE default), libretro entries carry their extracted core .so, standalone entries carry none.

vectors.name: catalogue-custom-overlay-replaces-system
vectors.rationale: A system defined in the custom_systems overlay replaces the bundled system of the same name entirely (ES-DE USERGUIDE, Game System Customizations).

vectors.name: catalogue-gamelist-selection-promotes-default
vectors.rationale: The user's saved per-system emulator choice lives in the gamelist.xml header as <alternativeEmulator><label> — written by ES-DE as two root elements (not well-formed XML, observed live). A matching label promotes that entry to effective default; the declared default stays as alternative.

vectors.name: catalogue-gamelist-selection-inside-gamelist-promotes-default
vectors.rationale: The same saved choice, written where ES-DE is moving it: <alternativeEmulator> as a child of <gameList> instead of a second root element (ES-DE reads both, document level first — GamelistFileParser.cpp:190-192; the nested shape is what RetroDECK 0.10.9b carries live). Where the element sits must not change which emulator atlas calls the effective default.

vectors.name: lrps2-shared-memcards-through-symlink
vectors.rationale: LRPS2's default (pcsx2_shared_memory_cards=enabled, libretro_core_options.h:169) keeps shared memory cards under <system_directory>/pcsx2/memcards. Under RetroDECK that path is a dir_prep symlink into the saves tree; the observed card is found through the link. The option's 'disabled' mode switches to per-game <rom_stem>.ps2 in the save directory (verified in libretro/ps2 source).

vectors.name: retrodeck-cfg-missing-platform-default-applies
vectors.rationale: A RetroDECK whose retroarch.cfg is missing: RetroArch initializes platform defaults before config load (platform_unix.c:2133-2134), so the effective root is 'saves' under the config tree — never the ROM's directory — and the upstream compile defaults govern sorting (sort_savefiles_enable=true, config.def.h:982).

vectors.name: entry-route-selection-to-placement
vectors.rationale: The natural client route: catalogue entry (with the gamelist selection applied) to its save placement in one ask. The promoted ParaLLEl entry resolves with its own core — the no-core caveat class does not exist on this path; the core is unaudited and the answer says so.

vectors.name: entry-route-standalone-is-unresolved
vectors.rationale: A standalone catalogue entry asked for its save location is a domain outcome with a stable code — outside current coverage, never a guess and never an exception.

vectors.name: secondary-handle-answers-its-own-config
vectors.rationale: Coexisting installations: the query names the native handle explicitly, and the answer comes from the native cfg alone — no cross-installation fall-through from the higher-priority RetroDECK.

vectors.name: retrodeck-marker-unreadable-is-present-and-broken
vectors.rationale: An unreadable marker is a PRESENT, broken RetroDECK — detection triggers on existence, and health separates the read failure from the root fallout instead of hiding the installation.

vectors.name: retrodeck-marker-invalid-json
vectors.rationale: Malformed JSON is not the same as an empty config object: the marker parses to nothing, health says marker-invalid, and the path fallbacks still answer.

vectors.name: a-roms-path-atlas-no-longer-reads-cannot-make-the-marker-invalid
vectors.rationale: roms_path is type-checked nowhere any more, because nothing reads it: the ROM root comes off ES-DE's own ROMDirectory, and retrodeck.json's copy is only the value RetroDECK seds into that setting. The scoping rule is that atlas reports on what it reads, so a key no read touches cannot make an installation unhealthy — reporting it would be a claim about who wrote the file. This machine is healthy with a roms_path that is not even a string, which is exactly the answer a marker-invalid finding here would get wrong.

vectors.name: sorted-dir-blocked-by-file-reverts-to-root
vectors.rationale: A file where the sorted directory belongs: RetroArch's mkdir MUST fail and it reverts to the unsorted root (runloop.c:8844) — the fallback is not conditional, it is the known answer.

files./mnt/sd/retrodeck/saves/gba: a file blocking the sorted dir

vectors.name: lrps2-dead-memcard-link-is-stated
vectors.rationale: The dir_prep link into an unmounted volume: the emulator-side memcards path is dead. The answer keeps the emulator-side directory and states the dead link with its target — physical_dir stays null because there is no existing backing path.

vectors.name: lrps2-memcard-link-cycle-is-stated
vectors.rationale: The other way a dir_prep link ends nowhere: the chain closes on itself, so the kernel answers ELOOP for the whole resolution rather than reaching any path at all. It is its own code next to dead-symlink because the two need different repairs — a dead link points at a name somebody can create, a cycle is one somebody has to break — and a consumer that branches only on dead-symlink to find an unwritable directory must miss this one. physical_dir stays null: there is no backing path, not even a half-resolved one to name.

vectors.name: emudeck-stale-marker-companion-missing
vectors.rationale: settings.sh survives while the claimed org.libretro.RetroArch Flatpak is gone: the EmuDeck handle stays (it claims the bare identity), and its health exposes the missing companion config instead of silently suppressing a bare handle.

vectors.name: opera-nvram-subdir-unanswered-when-no-mode-is-established
vectors.rationale: 3DO NVRAM (rule card 'opera') on a core the probe could not read: it loaded and answered, but registered no options this probe captured, so it declared no default for opera_nvram_storage. The opera card records none either — a default is written down only for a core that registers none, and this one normally does. With no options file on the machine, nothing states which mode is in force, so the card cannot pick between opera/per_game and opera/shared and steps aside rather than nesting a subdirectory on the strength of nothing. core-option-value-unestablished says which half is missing; the version comparison still runs and still reports that this card was never verified on any arrangement. The per_game answer this machine used to give lives on in opera-nvram-subdir-from-the-cores-own-default, where the core states its default.

vectors.name: opera-nvram-subdir-from-the-cores-own-default
vectors.rationale: The same 3DO machine with the core read as the shipped binary really answers: opera registers opera_nvram_storage and declares 'per game' as its default. No options file states a value, so that live default governs — a machine fact, not a recorded one — and the core nests opera/per_game under the effective save directory it receives from GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY (runloop.c:2001/8977). The file name carries the opera_nvram_version option, so the set is observed, never declared. The card was never live-verified on any arrangement, and the answer says so. This is the guarantee opera-nvram-subdir-unanswered-when-no-mode-is-established held while the card still carried a copy of the default.

vectors.name: opera-shared-nvram-subdir
vectors.rationale: The same core with opera_nvram_storage = shared switches to opera/shared with one card for every game — granularity and directory flip on one live-read option.

vectors.name: feature-detection-confirms-card-over-version-drift
vectors.rationale: The generation question decided by evidence, not version strings: the arrangement version drifted from the card's pin, but the probe shows the core REGISTERS the governing option with the card's value set — the card applies, no unverified-version alarm; the demotion is recorded in prose provenance (non-contractual). The arrangement-level tripwire is a different claim and still fires: observing one core option says nothing about whether the rest of atlas's RetroDECK knowledge still holds on 0.11.0, so the answer states that re-verification is pending while the placement itself stands.

vectors.name: multi-option-core-names-the-options-that-decide-granularity
vectors.rationale: SwanStation's audit verdict is multi-option: the directory follows the standard rule, but MemoryCards_Card1Type/Card2Type/UsePlaylistTitle decide whether the save is a per-game .srm, a serial- or title-keyed .mcd, or one card shared by every game. atlas does not interpret those options, so granularity stays null — and the caveat is what keeps that deliberate silence apart from a standard core's nothing-to-report, naming the options so a consumer can ask about them instead of assuming per-game.

vectors.name: standard-core-states-no-granularity-caveat
vectors.rationale: The negative control for the multi-option caveat, same layout and same empty granularity: mGBA's verdict is standard — RetroArch itself writes the save, per game, and nothing about the answer is being withheld. An empty caveat list here is what makes the multi-option caveat readable as 'deliberately unstated' rather than noise on every core.

vectors.name: standard-dir-core-observes-its-core-written-file-set
vectors.rationale: Beetle Saturn's verdict is standard-dir: the directory follows the rule and the file set is core-owned (.bcr/.bkr/.smpc, not RetroArch's .srm). No core option governs it — the shipped core registers none — so there is nothing deliberately unstated and no multi-option caveat: the files are content-keyed, the literal <rom_stem>.* observation reports all three, and the answer a per-game consumer reads is correct as it stands.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sandbox-override-dir-reaches-host
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK's RetroArch runs inside the Flatpak and writes its own spelling into the cfg: rgui_config_directory = "/var/config/retroarch/config", which Flatpak binds to ~/.var/app/<app id>/config/retroarch/config on the host (same inode, verified live). Translated, the stock config/PPSSPP/PPSSPP.cfg override is found and flips the layout flat; untranslated the whole override chain reads a directory that does not exist on the host.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sandbox-options-path-governs-card
vectors.rationale: core_options_path in the sandbox's spelling of the app config directory. The rule card's governing option is read from the file RetroArch would read, so the resolved granularity is shared-card; without the translation the file is invisible and the core default would stand in.

vectors.name: retrodeck-untranslatable-sandbox-path-is-stated
vectors.rationale: Same machine, but the override directory is configured under /var/db — inside the sandbox that is the runtime's own filesystem, which has no host location at all. The override cannot be read, so the sort-by-content layout stands, and the answer says why instead of presenting itself as complete.

vectors.name: ostree-home-under-var-is-not-a-sandbox-path
vectors.rationale: On an ostree host (Fedora Silverblue, Bazzite — both ship RetroDECK) /home is a symlink to /var/home, so real home directories live under /var. The machine's own configured directories must stay host paths there, while /var/config remains the sandbox bind of the app's config directory — which on this host resolves into that same /var/home. Both halves hold at once: the stock PPSSPP override is found through the sandbox spelling and flips the layout flat, and nothing is reported as untranslatable.

vectors.name: cfg-line-without-space-before-equals-is-dropped
vectors.rationale: A hand-edited cfg writes savefile_directory="…" with no space before the '='. RetroArch's key scan reads a run of isgraph characters, and '=' is one of them, so the key becomes the whole text and the line is refused (config_file.c:596-623): the saves root is NOT set, and the platform default under the config tree governs. Reading that line would attest a directory this RetroArch never writes to.

vectors.name: override-with-unknown-boolean-value-is-a-no-op
vectors.rationale: The core override spells sort_savefiles_by_content_enable = "yes". config_get_bool accepts exactly 1/true/0/false case-sensitively (config_file.c:1227-1262) and the bool loop writes nothing when it refuses (configuration.c:6412-6417), so the global layer's "true" still governs — the override does not turn the setting off. The rejected spelling is stated: nothing in the answer shows it otherwise.

vectors.name: cleared-rgui-config-directory-moves-overrides-one-level-up
vectors.rationale: rgui_config_directory = "default" clears the setting (configuration.c:6825-6826), and fill_pathname_application_special then falls back to the directory of the loaded retroarch.cfg (file_path_special.c:196-207) — one level above the platform default 'config' subdirectory. The override that governs is therefore <config dir>/PPSSPP/PPSSPP.cfg; the file in config/PPSSPP/ is the decoy that a wrong fallback would read.

vectors.name: app-relative-save-directory-is-stated-unexpanded
vectors.rationale: RetroArch's own config save writes ':' paths on some platforms: fill_pathname_expand_special resolves the prefix against the directory of the running RetroArch executable (file_path.c:1066-1101 → /proc/<pid>/exe, file_path.c:1421-1455). That directory is a property of the process, not of this disk, so atlas keeps the value as configured, states it, and does not run the existing-directory test on a path it would have had to invent.

vectors.name: unusable-override-save-root-keeps-the-global-root
vectors.rationale: The per-core override points savefile_directory at an unmounted card while the game override flips the sort. RetroArch merges the whole chain into one config and reloads the global cfg through it (configuration.c:7161-7243) WITHOUT config_set_defaults, so the value it refuses by path_is_directory (:6920) leaves the boot load's root standing - the global cfg's own /mnt/sd/retrodeck/saves, not the platform default. The rejection names the layer that stated it, because that is the file a caller has to fix.

vectors.name: override-switches-the-game-opt-layer-off
vectors.rationale: The per-core override sets game_specific_options = false. vectors.name: content-dir-root-and-sort-name-one-hole-once

vectors.name: trailing-slash-content-path-names-the-same-file

vectors.name: per-game-selection-reaches-the-game-that-declares-it

vectors.name: aggregate-an-empty-machine-answers-nothing
